notes: All venues are fictional. Ground truth follows guidelines v1.0 and was confirmed by human review. Frozen: create a new dataset version instead of editing these cases.

cases.description: Simple opening hours with no restricting qualifier.
cases.source_text: Bluefin Bakery opens every day from 7am to 3pm.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: Bluefin Bakery opens every day from 7am to 3pm.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Bluefin Bakery opens every day from 7am to 3pm.

cases.annotation_notes: Q1: 'every day' is the regular frequency, not an extra restriction, so scope is empty; normalized_statement must still keep 'every day'. Clock times are not scope.

cases.description: Opening hours limited to a season.
cases.source_text: During winter, the Old Pier Market is open from 10am to 6pm.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: During winter, the Old Pier Market is open from 10am to 6pm.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Old Pier Market is open from 10am to 6pm during winter.

cases.annotation_notes: The qualifier appears before the venue name; place_name drops the leading article.

cases.source_text: Casa Lume only accepts walk-ins and does not take bookings.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: Casa Lume only accepts walk-ins and does not take bookings.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Casa Lume only accepts walk-ins and does not take bookings.

cases.annotation_notes: Annotated as one claim; splitting into 'accepts walk-ins' and 'no bookings' would be redundant.

cases.description: Temporary closure with an end date.
cases.source_text: Lighthouse Tower is closed for renovation until 30 April 2027.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: Lighthouse Tower is closed for renovation until 30 April 2027.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Lighthouse Tower is closed for renovation until 30 April 2027.

cases.annotation_notes: C2: the closure end date is scope. The real-API smoke test returned scope null for this sentence.

cases.description: Venue named only in a heading; pronoun claims about opening days and a weekly and holiday rest schedule.
cases.source_text:
Harbour Tile Museum

It is open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 5pm. It is closed on Mondays and public holidays.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: It is open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 5pm.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Harbour Tile Museum is open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 5pm.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: It is closed on Mondays and public holidays.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Harbour Tile Museum is closed on Mondays and public holidays.

cases.annotation_notes: Excerpts do not contain the venue name; place_name comes from the heading. C3: weekly and public-holiday rest days are opening_hours, not closure. C1: operating days are scope. 'on Mondays and public holidays' is one coordinated qualifier and stays a single scope item (Q3).

cases.description: Personal observation that must not become a recurring rule.
cases.source_text: We visited Taberna Azul on a Monday and it was open.

expected_skipped.original_excerpt: We visited Taberna Azul on a Monday and it was open.

cases.annotation_notes: Mirrors AC-04. Returning nothing at all is also acceptable behaviour, but the expected output is a skipped observation.

cases.description: Factual statements outside the supported claim types.
cases.source_text: A coffee at Bluefin Bakery costs 2 euros. Bluefin Bakery only accepts cash.

expected_skipped.original_excerpt: A coffee at Bluefin Bakery costs 2 euros.

cases.annotation_notes: Mirrors AC-06 (price) and adds a payment-method claim.

cases.description: Subjective opinions only; nothing should be extracted.
cases.source_text: The rooftop terrace at Hotel Miradouro has the best sunset view in the city. The staff are wonderfully friendly.
must_not_extract: The rooftop terrace at Hotel Miradouro has the best sunset view in the city.
cases.annotation_notes: Any accepted claim, including one from these sentences, is a false positive. Candidates that post-processing skips are diagnostic only.

cases.description: Several claims about two venues, with context-based place names.
cases.source_text: Mercado Norte is open Monday to Saturday from 8am to 2pm. Its upstairs restaurant, Sala Norte, requires a reservation for dinner. Sala Norte is closed for refurbishment from 1 to 21 August 2027.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: Mercado Norte is open Monday to Saturday from 8am to 2pm.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Mercado Norte is open Monday to Saturday from 8am to 2pm.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: Its upstairs restaurant, Sala Norte, requires a reservation for dinner.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Sala Norte requires a reservation for dinner.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: Sala Norte is closed for refurbishment from 1 to 21 August 2027.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Sala Norte is closed for refurbishment from 1 to 21 August 2027.

cases.annotation_notes: The reservation applies to Sala Norte, not Mercado Norte. 'upstairs restaurant' is description, not a claim. C3: a dated refurbishment is a specific closure event. C1/C2: operating days and the closure period are scope.

cases.description: Conditional reservation rule whose condition is easy to omit.
cases.source_text: At Casa Lume, reservations are only required for groups of six or more.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: At Casa Lume, reservations are only required for groups of six or more.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Casa Lume requires reservations only for groups of six or more.
scope: for groups of six or more

cases.annotation_notes: Tests rule 7 of the guidelines: 'Casa Lume requires reservations' with scope null is detected but semantically wrong.

cases.description: One reservation rule restricted by two independent qualifiers.
cases.source_text: On weekends, Adega Serena requires reservations during summer.

expected_claims.original_excerpt: On weekends, Adega Serena requires reservations during summer.
expected_claims.normalized_statement: Adega Serena requires reservations on weekends during summer.

cases.annotation_notes: Q3: the two qualifiers are stated separately and both apply (AND), so they are separate scope items. Omitting either one broadens the rule and fails scope. A single combined item such as 'on weekends during summer' is semantically equivalent.
